findings.title: The envier becomes dangerous when the disposition acts
findings.claim: The repeated focus form presents harm as a transition: the person marked by removal-seeking envy becomes the source of harm when that envy takes effect against another's good.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries the accepted removal-seeking sense in حَاسِدٍ and repeats it as حَسَدَ; إِذَا supplies the conditional threshold, while the supplied hasad connection rows provide wider instances of envy as harm directed through a person.
findings.reader_payoff: The refuge phrase can be heard as reaching the envier at the point where an inward hostile disposition becomes an active attempt to remove another's good, while the ordinary refuge meaning remains recoverable.
findings.containment: The packet supports a threshold reading, not a universal claim that every envier acts. The connection rows supply target Arabic and relation notes without target morphology, so no further grammatical detail is inferred from them.

epistemic.reason: A trusted focus finding and the focus morphology ground the relation; the wider return is corroborated by a legacy reader walk and connection rows whose target morphology is explicitly absent.

branch_activations.carrier: The focus forms حَاسِدٍ and حَسَدَ carry the accepted relation of wanting another person's good to leave that person.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The particle إِذَا marks conditional activation, and the supplied 2:109 and 114:1 connection rows return the wider idea of hasad as harm directed through an envier.
branch_activations.activation: The repeated carrier meets the conditional relation and the wider hasad parallels, making a disposition entering effective conduct perceptible without replacing the plain refuge request.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Protection is sought from removal-seeking envy at the moment it becomes operative against another's good.
branch_activations.boundary: This does not make every person described as envious an actor and does not infer missing morphology for the connection targets.

findings.title: Comparison keeps two directions visible
findings.claim: The focus preserves a distinction between wanting a like good for oneself and wanting the other person's good to disappear; the harm frame makes the second direction the danger while keeping the first as a live lexical boundary.
findings.mechanism: The two accepted Hsd facets meet the independent شَرِّ occurrence: root_000319/B002 carries non-dispossessive emulation, root_000319/B001 carries removal-seeking envy, and root_000787/B001 supplies the focus's evil frame. The supplied connection contrast keeps accusation and harm from being treated as interchangeable.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clause becomes precise about what the refuge names: comparison itself is not flattened into harm; the turn toward another's loss is what gives the threat its destructive direction.
findings.containment: B002 is carried as a contrastive contextual resonance, not as a claim that benign emulation is itself the harm named by the refuge. The wide-walk س م و/B007 citation remains unresolved, and no additional upward-rivalry branch is asserted.

epistemic.reason: The distinction is stated by a trusted publication and supported by accepted focus branch records; the wider comparison extensions come from legacy reader walks and remain qualified.

findings.title: Envy aims at bestowed flourishing
findings.claim: The envier's target can be seen as another person's bestowed and sustained flourishing: a good brought forth and cared for becomes the object of an attempt to have it removed.
findings.mechanism: The Hsd B001 carrier is placed against the supplied pericope movement of mercy, nurture, creation, and preservation; the independent earlier context turns envy from a private comparison into a will directed at undoing another's received good.
findings.reader_payoff: The final person in the refuge sequence becomes a threat to a recipient's flourishing, so the harm is perceptible as an attempted reversal of care rather than as an unlocated hostile feeling.
findings.containment: The context joins are supplied at ayah-level and the reader sources cite unresolved ر ح م/B001 material; this finding does not assert that envy attacks divine agency, that one agent caused every earlier threat, or that every good is literally a mercy gift.

epistemic.reason: A trusted publication supplies the removal-of-bestowed-good relation, while legacy reader walks supply the mercy and nurture framing without a complete word-level crosswalk.

findings.title: Removal-seeking envy finds outward channels
findings.claim: The focus's removal-seeking envy can be read as an inward intention that becomes harmful through outward channels already named in the preceding threat sequence: concealed entry, breath or speech, and binding.
findings.mechanism: The Hsd B001 carrier returns through the exact pericope ayahs 113:3-4 and the supplied refuge connections from inward prompting, so the final act can gather earlier mechanisms as possible ways a hostile intention takes effect.
findings.reader_payoff: The final clause becomes connected to concrete modes of harm: an inward contraction may issue through a word, breath, knot, report, or hidden ingress, making the envier an intelligible source for the prior threat images.
findings.containment: The packet does not identify one agent across 113:3-4 and does not decide among literal ritual, interpersonal speech, reputational circulation, or psychophysical discharge. These remain coexisting attributed possibilities, not a single asserted mechanism.

epistemic.reason: The trusted cross-run finding supplies the focus branch and named channels; legacy reader walks and refuge connections supply the wider return but explicitly leave agent identity and modality open.

findings.title: The final envier gathers earlier threat mechanisms
findings.claim: On rereading the whole supplied pericope, the final envier can function as a personal condensation of the earlier sequence: hidden darkness, outward emission, and binding become possible operations of a will that seeks another's good to disappear.
findings.mechanism: The Hsd B001 carrier in the final ayah returns through the earlier 113:3-4 mechanisms named by the retrospective source, so separate threat images can be gathered under a possible human source without being reduced to it.
findings.reader_payoff: The ending acquires a retrospective human focus: what appeared as separate hidden or emitted harms can also be perceived as the outward history of a removal-seeking intention.
findings.containment: This is a single legacy reader's exploratory synthesis. The packet supplies no later ayah after 113:5, no complete word-level crosswalk for every earlier root, and no identification of one agent; the gathering remains a possible rereading.

epistemic.reason: The retrospective reader-walk text directly states the changed whole-pericope view, but its branch and context joins are attributed rather than independently crosswalked.
